solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Grilling, or being fried, possibly

indicators.note: 'possibly' says the words could be something else, so the letters of 'being fried' may take another form

explanation.surface: A cook weighs up two ways of preparing something: under the grill or in the frying pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grilling' looks like cookery, but here it is questioning someone closely, as happens to an agent back from a mission.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the informal sense: grilling someone is questioning them hard, just as officials do when a mission ends.

clue.text: Club record with vocoder in the middle

indicators.note: 'in the middle' points at the centre of the word, so only the fourth of the seven letters of 'vocoder' is used

parts.note: the fourth of its seven letters, v-o-c-O-d-e-r

explanation.surface: A club DJ plays a record featuring a voice run through a vocoder.
explanation.walkthrough: A vocoder is the robotic voice effect heard on dance records, which fits the club scene nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a club where people go to dance to recorded music.

clue.text: Uncle and boys act out something at a kid's party?

indicators.note: 'act out' suggests performing, but 'out' also means out of order, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: the letters to rearrange; 'and' just joins the words

explanation.surface: An uncle and some boys put on a performance at a child's birthday party.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is only an example: this is one thing you might find at a children's party.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an inflatable play structure is often hired for children's parties.

clue.text: Passage lacking a key

indicators.note: something lacking an item goes without it, so the passage loses its A

parts.note: a passage between rows of seats

explanation.surface: A corridor that cannot be opened because nobody has a key for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A key' looks like a musical key or one for a lock; the 'a' is the letter taken out, and a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A less familiar sense: a key, or cay, is a small low island, as in the Florida Keys.

clue.text: In favour of proposed ban

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it
to bid is to offer or propose

explanation.surface: Someone supports a ban that has been put forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one opinion about a new ban; in fact 'ban' is the definition and the rest is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to prohibit something.

clue.text: Well-organised European suppressing a US revolt

parts.note: taken as written, placed after the N

explanation.surface: An orderly European official puts down an American uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolt' reads as a noun, an uprising; it is the verb, to disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: to revolt someone is to sicken or disgust them.

clue.text: Male writer such as JRR Tolkien or DBC Pierre?

definitions.meaning: each goes by a string of three initials

explanation.surface: Two authors known by strings of initials are offered as examples of male writers.
explanation.walkthrough: Both are real writers, which keeps the surface honest, but the joke is their names: each carries three initials, so each is literally a man with letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a literary scholar or writer, and read literally it fits men whose names are mostly initials.

clue.text: Continue working after wicked uprising

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means reading upwards
'after' puts one piece later than another

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone keeps working in the aftermath of a wicked rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprising' looks like a revolt; in a down clue it tells you to read the wickedness from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to carry on existing, as a memory or legacy continues.

clue.text: Filth, look, fills plaza almost entirely

indicators.note: something that fills a space sits inside it
'almost' stops just short of the whole, so the plaza word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Rubbish, look, is filling almost the whole of a town plaza.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas make 'look' an aside to the reader, but it is a piece of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a state of dirt and wretched neglect.

clue.text: Some monosodium — a mightily savoury taste

indicators.note: 'some' means only part, so only part of the letters of the following words is used

parts.note: the last two letters of 'monosodium', then 'a', then the first two of 'mightily'

explanation.surface: Monosodium glutamate gives food a powerful savoury flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to monosodium glutamate, the flavour enhancer that delivers exactly this taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain definition: the Japanese name for the fifth basic taste, the savoury one found in broths and aged cheese.

clue.text: Contact striking the head that hurts!

indicators.note: to strike something is to cross it out, as in striking a word from the record, so the first letter goes

explanation.surface: A blow lands on someone's head and they cry out in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking the head' reads as a blow to the skull; it means deleting the head letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is a paraphrase of the exclamation itself: it is what you cry when something hurts.

clue.text: Exasperating book containing anger and spite primarily

indicators.note: a thing containing others holds them inside

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: 'primarily' means first of all, so only the first letter of 'spite' is used

explanation.surface: A maddening book full of rage and malice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exasperating' could describe the book, but it stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: annoying and wearing on the patience.

clue.text: Principle of harmonious design for which iron is hung in pieces

indicators.note: something in pieces is broken up, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Some design philosophy calls for iron to be displayed in fragments.
explanation.walkthrough: FE happens to stay in place at the front; only the letters of 'is hung' really move.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain definition: the Chinese practice of arranging buildings and rooms so they are in harmony with their surroundings.

clue.text: Hidden store of money picked up

indicators.note: a sound is picked up by the ear, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: notes and coins; the French-derived spelling says the same

explanation.surface: Someone finds a secret stash of money and takes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' reads as collecting the loot; it refers to hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain definition: a secret stock of supplies or valuables.

clue.text: Grass and concrete beneath church

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is beneath comes later

parts.note: concrete in the sense of real, tangible

explanation.surface: A churchyard has lawn and a slab of concrete under the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concrete' reads as the building material; it is the adjective meaning actual.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: wheat, barley and oats are grasses grown for their grain.

clue.text: Piece of felt alongside cards laid on a table

indicators.note: a piece is only part of the whole, so only part of 'felt alongside' is used

parts.note: the last letter of 'felt' and the first four of 'alongside'

explanation.surface: A card game on a baize table, with cards set down beside a patch of felt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of felt' looks like the baize itself; it marks the letters taken from the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A card-game term: the stock of undealt cards left on the table after the deal.

clue.text: Someone who is unkind — that is to say, below average

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is below comes later

explanation.surface: An unkind person is judged to be, in other words, not up to scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below average' reads as a verdict of poor quality; it places one piece underneath the other.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal noun for a spiteful or ungenerous person.

clue.text: Quit a job, or agreed to a new contract?

definitions.meaning: signed again, with the prefix meaning 'again'

explanation.surface: An employee either left or stayed on under fresh terms.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: the same letters mean left the job and, split after the RE, signed the contract again.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the past tense of leaving a post, and a hyphen-free spelling of signing once more.

clue.text: In a higher position at work

parts.note: op., short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone has been promoted to a senior post in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At work' reads as a single phrase about the office, and 'In a higher position' as promotion; it means physically on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: on top of, above.

clue.text: Devotion and compassion holding true in the end

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside
'in the end' points to the final letter of 'true'

explanation.surface: Faith and mercy remain constant to the last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding true' reads as staying faithful; the words split into an instruction and a letter source.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: religious devotion and reverence.

clue.text: Double whiskey in metal receptacle

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a tin is a metal container
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A double measure of whiskey is served in a metal cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double whiskey' reads as a bar order; 'Double' is the definition and the drink is just one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone's double is their exact counterpart.

clue.text: Everybody has almost rejected God

indicators.note: 'almost' stops just short, so HAS loses its last letter
something rejected is sent back

explanation.surface: Nearly everyone has turned away from God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' looks like a linking verb; it is wordplay, trimmed and turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain definition: the Arabic name for God, used in Islam.

clue.text: Erewhon's about non-existent place

indicators.note: things moved about are scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that Samuel Butler's novel Erewhon is about an imaginary country.
explanation.walkthrough: Erewhon, Samuel Butler's satire set in a fictional land, took its title from this very anagram, so the surface is literally true.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain definition: the word for a place that does not exist, which Butler's title spells backwards.

clue.text: Don't say I've changed, it may be scary to behold

definitions.text: it may be scary to behold

indicators.note: something changed takes a new form, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, ignoring the apostrophes

explanation.surface: Someone insists they haven't changed, though their new look is frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a British term from the 1980s for a violent horror film on videotape.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a gory horror film, certainly scary to watch.
